properties.name: 100 Statistical Tests In R
properties.description: Comprehensive guide to 100 statistical tests implemented in R, organized by category: comparison of means, proportions, variances, correlation, regression diagnostics, normality, and non-parametric tests

properties.name: One Sample t-Test
properties.description: Tests whether the mean of a single sample differs from a specified value
properties.null_hypothesis: μ = μ₀ (population mean equals hypothesized value)
properties.alternative_hypothesis: μ ≠ μ₀ (two-sided) or μ > μ₀ or μ < μ₀ (one-sided)
properties.interpretation_guide: If p-value < α, reject H₀. The sample mean significantly differs from the hypothesized value.

properties.name: Two Sample t-Test (Independent)
properties.description: Compares means of two independent groups
properties.null_hypothesis: μ₁ = μ₂ (both population means are equal)
properties.interpretation_guide: If p-value < α, conclude the means differ significantly.

properties.name: Paired t-Test
properties.description: Compares means of two related samples (before-after, matched pairs)
properties.interpretation_guide: If p-value < α, the treatment had a significant effect.

properties.name: Welch's t-Test
properties.description: Two-sample t-test that does not assume equal variances
properties.interpretation_guide: Preferred over Student's t-test when variances differ.

properties.name: One-Way ANOVA
properties.description: Compares means across three or more independent groups
properties.null_hypothesis: μ₁ = μ₂ = ... = μk (all group means are equal)
properties.test_statistic: F = MSB / MSW (between-group vs within-group variance)
properties.interpretation_guide: If F is significant, use post-hoc tests (Tukey, Bonferroni) to identify which groups differ.

properties.name: Two-Way ANOVA
properties.description: Tests effects of two factors and their interaction on a continuous outcome
properties.null_hypothesis: No main effects and no interaction
properties.alternative_hypothesis: At least one effect is significant
properties.test_statistic: F statistics for each factor and interaction
properties.interpretation_guide: Interpret interaction first; if significant, main effects may be misleading.

properties.name: Kruskal-Wallis Test
properties.description: Non-parametric alternative to one-way ANOVA for comparing medians across groups
properties.null_hypothesis: All groups have the same distribution
properties.interpretation_guide: Use when normality assumption is violated. Follow up with Dunn's test for pairwise comparisons.

properties.name: Mann-Whitney U Test (Wilcoxon Rank-Sum)
properties.description: Non-parametric alternative to independent two-sample t-test
properties.null_hypothesis: Both groups have the same distribution
properties.test_statistic: U or W statistic based on ranks
properties.interpretation_guide: Use when data is non-normal or ordinal.

properties.name: Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test
properties.description: Non-parametric alternative to paired t-test
properties.test_statistic: V statistic based on signed ranks
properties.interpretation_guide: Use for paired data when normality is questionable.

properties.name: Shapiro-Wilk Normality Test
properties.description: Tests whether a sample comes from a normally distributed population
properties.interpretation_guide: If p < α, reject normality. High power for detecting non-normality. Preferred for small samples.

properties.name: Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test
properties.description: Tests whether a sample follows a specified distribution or compares two samples
properties.null_hypothesis: Sample follows the specified distribution (one-sample) or both samples come from same distribution (two-sample)
properties.r_syntax:
ks.test(x, 'pnorm', mean, sd) # one-sample
ks.test(x, y) # two-sample
assumptions: Parameters must be specified, not estimated
properties.interpretation_guide: Sensitive to differences in location, scale, and shape. Less powerful than Shapiro-Wilk for normality.

properties.name: Anderson-Darling Test
properties.description: Tests goodness of fit with more weight on tails than KS test
properties.alternative_hypothesis: Data does not follow the distribution
properties.interpretation_guide: More sensitive to tail deviations than KS test. Good for detecting departures in extremes.

properties.name: Jarque-Bera Test
properties.description: Tests normality based on skewness and kurtosis
properties.null_hypothesis: Data is normally distributed (skewness=0, excess kurtosis=0)
properties.interpretation_guide: Common in econometrics for regression residuals. Requires n > 30 for reliable results.

properties.name: Levene's Test
properties.description: Tests equality of variances across groups
properties.null_hypothesis: σ₁² = σ₂² = ... = σk² (all group variances are equal)
properties.test_statistic: F statistic based on absolute deviations from group medians
properties.interpretation_guide: Use before ANOVA. More robust than Bartlett's test when normality is violated.

properties.name: Bartlett's Test
properties.description: Tests equality of variances across groups
properties.interpretation_guide: Very sensitive to non-normality. Prefer Levene's test if normality is questionable.

properties.name: F-Test for Variance Ratio
properties.description: Compares variances of two samples
properties.interpretation_guide: Very sensitive to non-normality. Consider Levene's test as alternative.

properties.name: Chi-Squared Goodness of Fit
properties.description: Tests whether observed frequencies match expected frequencies
properties.interpretation_guide: If expected counts < 5, use exact tests or combine categories.

properties.name: Chi-Squared Test of Independence
properties.description: Tests whether two categorical variables are independent
properties.interpretation_guide: For 2x2 tables, use Yates' correction or Fisher's exact test.

properties.name: Fisher's Exact Test
properties.description: Exact test for independence in 2x2 contingency tables
properties.test_statistic: Exact probability based on hypergeometric distribution
properties.interpretation_guide: Preferred over chi-squared for small samples or when expected counts < 5.

properties.name: McNemar's Test
properties.description: Tests for changes in proportions in paired categorical data
properties.test_statistic: χ² = (b-c)²/(b+c) for off-diagonal cells b and c
properties.interpretation_guide: Common in before-after studies. For small samples, use exact version.

properties.name: Pearson Correlation Test
properties.description: Tests whether linear correlation between two variables is significant
properties.interpretation_guide: r ranges from -1 to 1. |r| > 0.7 strong, 0.3-0.7 moderate, < 0.3 weak.

properties.name: Spearman Rank Correlation Test
properties.description: Non-parametric test for monotonic relationship between variables
properties.interpretation_guide: Use when data is non-normal or relationship is monotonic but not linear.

properties.name: Kendall's Tau Correlation Test
properties.description: Non-parametric test based on concordant and discordant pairs
properties.interpretation_guide: More robust than Spearman for small samples and ties. τ values are typically smaller than r.

properties.name: Durbin-Watson Test
properties.description: Tests for first-order autocorrelation in regression residuals
properties.interpretation_guide: DW ≈ 2 suggests no autocorrelation. DW < 2 positive, DW > 2 negative. Check dL and dU tables.

properties.name: Breusch-Godfrey Test
properties.description: Tests for higher-order serial correlation in regression residuals
properties.null_hypothesis: No serial correlation up to order p
properties.interpretation_guide: More general than Durbin-Watson. Can test for AR(p) and MA(q) processes.

properties.name: Breusch-Pagan Test
properties.description: Tests for heteroscedasticity in regression residuals
properties.test_statistic: LM = nR² from auxiliary regression of squared residuals
properties.interpretation_guide: If rejected, use robust standard errors (HC) or weighted least squares.

properties.name: White's Test
properties.description: General test for heteroscedasticity without assuming functional form
properties.test_statistic: nR² from auxiliary regression with squares and cross-products
properties.interpretation_guide: More general than Breusch-Pagan. Does not assume specific form of heteroscedasticity.

properties.name: RESET Test (Ramsey)
properties.description: Tests for functional form misspecification in regression
properties.interpretation_guide: If rejected, consider adding polynomial terms, interactions, or transformations.

properties.name: Variance Inflation Factor (VIF)
properties.description: Detects multicollinearity among predictor variables
properties.interpretation_guide: VIF > 5 suggests concern, VIF > 10 indicates severe multicollinearity. Consider dropping or combining variables.

properties.name: Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
properties.description: Tests for unit root (non-stationarity) in time series
properties.test_statistic: t-statistic on lagged level in augmented regression
properties.r_function: adf.test() from tseries, ur.df() from urca
properties.r_syntax:
library(tseries); adf.test(x)
library(urca); ur.df(x, type='drift', lags=4)
properties.interpretation_guide: If p > α, cannot reject unit root. Series needs differencing. Critical values differ from standard t.

properties.name: KPSS Test
properties.description: Tests for stationarity (opposite null hypothesis to ADF)
properties.interpretation_guide: Use together with ADF. If ADF rejects and KPSS doesn't reject, series is stationary.

properties.name: Phillips-Perron Test
properties.description: Non-parametric unit root test robust to serial correlation
properties.interpretation_guide: More robust than ADF to heteroscedasticity and serial correlation in errors.

properties.name: Ljung-Box Test
properties.description: Tests for autocorrelation in time series or regression residuals
properties.null_hypothesis: No autocorrelation up to lag h
properties.interpretation_guide: Common diagnostic for ARIMA residuals. If rejected, model may need more AR or MA terms.

properties.name: Granger Causality Test
properties.description: Tests whether one time series helps predict another
properties.alternative_hypothesis: X Granger-causes Y (X improves prediction of Y)
properties.interpretation_guide: Statistical causality, not true causality. Test both directions. Sensitive to lag selection.

properties.name: Johansen Cointegration Test
properties.description: Tests for cointegration among multiple time series
properties.test_statistic: Trace statistic and Maximum Eigenvalue statistic
properties.interpretation_guide: If cointegration exists, use VECM instead of VAR in differences.

properties.name: Runs Test (Wald-Wolfowitz)
properties.description: Tests randomness of a sequence
properties.test_statistic: Number of runs compared to expected under randomness
properties.interpretation_guide: Too few runs suggests clustering, too many suggests alternation.

properties.name: Binomial Test
properties.description: Tests whether proportion differs from hypothesized value
properties.interpretation_guide: Exact test, no large-sample approximation needed. Preferred for small samples.

properties.name: One-Sample Proportion Test
properties.description: Tests whether sample proportion differs from hypothesized value
properties.interpretation_guide: Large-sample approximation. For small samples, use exact binomial test.

properties.name: Two-Sample Proportion Test
properties.description: Compares proportions between two independent groups
properties.interpretation_guide: For small samples, use Fisher's exact test.

properties.name: Sign Test
properties.description: Non-parametric test for median based on signs of differences
properties.interpretation_guide: Very robust but less powerful than Wilcoxon. Use when distribution is highly skewed.

properties.name: Friedman Test
properties.description: Non-parametric alternative to repeated measures ANOVA
properties.null_hypothesis: All treatments have the same effect
properties.test_statistic: χ² based on ranks within blocks
properties.interpretation_guide: Use when normality assumption of repeated measures ANOVA is violated.
